title: [Issue]: After updating to 10.9.0, the live TV feature has a failure to play error
body:
### Please describe your bug

After the update, the M3C live feed cannot be played, indicating a fatal error or server error, which did not exist before the update.

### Reproduction Steps

1. Web player/Android client player 
2, start playing a program
 3, after loading for a period of time, the player fatal error prompt pops up

### Jellyfin Version

10.9.0

### if other:

_No response_

comments.body: Had exactly the same issue. Had to go back to 10.3.13. Too bad such important functionality has not been tested.

comments.author: participant3
comments.body: It is up to everyone to test unstable releases leading up to a new stable release and report any new issues to ensure regressions do not occur. It is impossible for the Jellyfin team to test every variation of people's configurations in existence. For me and my live tv setup, 10.9.0 seems to work without issue.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
> It is up to everyone to test unstable releases leading up to a new stable release and report any new issues to ensure regressions do not occur. It is impossible for the Jellyfin team to test every variation of people's configurations in existence. For me and my live tv setup, 10.9.0 seems to work without issue.

I would assume that we do have substantial test cases that run before the release. If not I highly recommend we start developing them and run these through every time there is changes. This is standard dev practice. You do not wait for clients to test and get back to you. 

Test cases are written and developed when new functionality is added to the code. Oh, I forgot that you did not know that. We old guys who retired coding spend decades doing that. But now I guess we dont.

comments.author: participant4
comments.body:
> > It is up to everyone to test unstable releases leading up to a new stable release and report any new issues to ensure regressions do not occur. It is impossible for the Jellyfin team to test every variation of people's configurations in existence. For me and my live tv setup, 10.9.0 seems to work without issue.
> 
> I would assume that we do have substantial test cases that run before the release. If not I highly recommend we start developing them and run these through every time there is changes. This is standard dev practice. You do not wait for clients to test and get back to you.
> 
> Test cases are written and developed when new functionality is added to the code. Oh, I forgot that you did not know that. We old guys who retired coding spend decades doing that. But now I guess we dont.

LiveTV is extremely hard to test with due to the fact that TV providers and TV tuners usually breaks the spec in this way and that way, and the problem is probably hard to identify until you are testing against real channels. The LiveTV feature itself is made of "supposed to work" way plus a lot of workarounds for specific TV providers. For example #11496 for some TV Tuners do not implement HTTP HEAD method.

comments.author: participant5
comments.body:
> I would assume that we do have substantial test cases that run before the release. If not I highly recommend we start developing them and run these through every time there is changes. This is standard dev practice. You do not wait for clients to test and get back to you.

The project has a lot of inherited functionality, and obviously not all of them have automatic testing. Everyone is free to work on the features they consider important. If LiveTV is so important to you, write these tests, help the project.

I've got one remote user with no issues on a Fire TV Stick (not really tech savvy).

Another remote fire stick user reports out of sync audio, which I can also confirm for LG WebOS TV on the LAN as well. 

I can watch on Android, but get a Source Error on the first playback attempt. Second attempt is fine. Audio remains in sync. 

Recordings are outright borked. Attempting to manage them results in endless spin and seems to completely crash the server, have to restart it to even be able to log back in again. 

None of these issues were present in 10.8.13. 

I will gather some relevant logs if I can.

comments.author: participant4
comments.body:
> I had no words anymore. 10.9.2 was fine with Live TV and all my stream would easly remux to my Firefox client. After upgrade to 10.9.3 all streams (9) would transcode now. Going back until developers figure this out how to properly do this.

Please see https://github.com/jellyfin/jellyfin/issues/11847 for why we made this change.

This is a hard choice for us but we cannot make everybody happy because TV Tuners have not predictable behavior and the current only way to make it work for most people is to do something like this. The only reliable way that can make everybody happy is to expose enough options and let the user try and fail instead of server-side guessing, because it is impossible to always guess it right.

>  I think you should be aiming to do everything possible to avoid transcoding.

I want to do this as much as you do. But the TV tuners leave us no choice because we cannot even reliably detect what the source stream format is in, and the incorrect detection directly failed playback for some users. It worked for you but not for everyone. 

> As a alternative you can offer both options to the users Option A (from 10.9.2) and Option B (10.9.3).

We can do even better than this and provide even more configuration. But this would introduce an API change and that is not something usually happens during patch releases. If most of the team agrees that we can make exceptions for LiveTV to have API changes in 10.9 then we can add options to control the behavior for 10.9.

> I dont know what other users do use but I would encourage you to test your code against some of the most popular Live TV channels and using reputable LIve TV channels/providers.

It is not that simple because even the "reputable providers" are doing things wrong and it does not even cover most of the potential use cases.

> There are plenty of resources out there to help you build a good test cases with many diverse configurations.

There are not. Because they are too divergent. Even the detection of the stream type is a mission impossible. The standard defined way to check if a stream is an HLS stream or MPEG-TS stream is to check the mime type. But we cannot do it for TV Tuners, because their http server implementation does not bother to return the correct mime type. Can we tell from the file extension like `.ts` or `.m3u8`? No we still cannot, because a lot of tuner's url is just ip and port, and does not have any file extension in that. So the only way to detect stream type is now actually fetch that url and analyze the content, which is less than ideal and also painfully slow. Hope you understand the situation better with this example, and this is only one of the quirks that we have to deal with.

comments.author: participant4
comments.body:
If I can add options I would already add it. The problem is adding option means API change which is usually prohibited during patch releases. If I don't do something like this you won't get livetv working in 10.9.2, you will have a broken one until 10.10. I know the best way to make livetv cover more use cases is to add more options, I know it since the first glance at the code and know why it breaks. But I have to also find some way that can be merged into 10.9 branch so that affected users don't have to wait for months for a new major release.

> and both are related to HDHomeRun and you decided to limit to 20Mb with this value being hardcoded.

Please don't make judgments without knowing the whole picture. This is not HDHomeRun specific, and 20Mb is a very high bitrate for live streams, higher than what Netflix uses. Browsers like Firefox won't play live streams with too high a bitrate, and hardware encoders like the ones in low-end Intel CPUs will fail when transcoding at very high bitrates. The reporter used HDHomeRun does not mean this problem only applies to HDHomeRun. I have to set a safe upper limit hard-coded because it is the only way to avoid introducing an API change while still addressing the too-high bitrate issue for our users.
